overall_assessment.realism: The samples are highly realistic, reflecting common spear phishing tactics such as domain spoofing, use of newly registered domains with privacy protection, embedding malicious payloads (HTML forms, macro-enabled attachments, malicious PDFs), and social engineering techniques like urgency and impersonation of trusted entities. The technical details including email headers, SMTP transaction logs, domain WHOIS data, network captures, and process logs are detailed and plausible, enhancing authenticity. The inclusion of specific MITRE ATT&CK techniques further grounds the scenarios in real-world threat frameworks.
overall_assessment.consistency: The dataset is consistent and adheres well to a clear schema across all samples. Each entry contains a scenario description, detailed technical data with relevant fields (email headers, body, attachments, domain registration info, network logs), indicators, detection methods, and relevant MITRE techniques. Field naming is uniform, and data types are appropriate. Minor variations in field presence (e.g., some have 'powershell_script_snippet' as empty string or null) are acceptable given scenario differences but remain consistent in structure.
suggestions: Standardize null or empty fields consistently (e.g., use null instead of empty string for absent data) to improve parsing.
Include explicit fields for email content type (e.g., 'text/plain', 'text/html') in all samples for clarity.
Add more examples of URL obfuscation techniques (e.g., use of homoglyphs, URL shorteners) to diversify tactics.
Incorporate sender IP geolocation or ASN info in suspicious domain registration or email headers to enrich context.
Provide example user responses or incident outcomes to illustrate impact and detection efficacy.
Consider adding a unique identifier field per sample for easier referencing and indexing.
